proposed_core_edits.reason: The displayed instance itself gives \(1\le r_{3,1}=1<3\), \(1\le r_{3,2}=2<3\), and \(r_{3,1}\ne r_{3,2}\). The proof uses bounded outcomes for the contrast-neighborhood Lipschitz bound, but it uses no condition on treated-count entries at other cluster sizes. This replacement removes the two redundant global assumption edges and records the actually used bounded-outcome premise without changing the claim.

proposed.statement: For two size-three clusters, \(K=2\), \(r_{3,1}=1\), \(r_{3,2}=2\), and coefficient order \((c_{1,1},c_{0,1},c_{1,2},c_{0,2})=(3,-1,-1,-1)\), a rational 78-decision procedure and a 17-orbit prior certify \(1.3649753<R^\star\le1.364981422\) with primal-dual gap below \(10^{-5}\), while a 15-orbit prior certifies \(R_{\mathrm{ind}}>1.3659\). Thus \(R_{\mathrm{ind}}-R^\star>0.000918578\). For every rational \(t\) with \(|t|\le10^{-5}\), replacing \(c\) by \((3+t,-1-t,-1,-1)\) preserves \(R_{\mathrm{ind}}-R^\star>7\times10^{-4}\).
proposed.justification: The rational separation proves that cross-cluster correlation can lower unrestricted minimax risk, not merely the variance of a selected linear estimator.
proposed.gap: Hull2026's independent-design theorem relies on a no-interference tensorization, and CaiPougetAbadieAiroldi2022 optimizes a conventional estimator; the certified saturation instance permits every measurable estimator on both sides.
proposed.consumer: The result supplies a concrete reason for BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018-style trials to consider correlated saturation labels when robust finite-population MSE is the design criterion.
